newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hog prices seen mixed - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen mixed, depending on hog supplies and plans for Saturday operations, livestock dealers said.

Warmer temperatures were expected to replace Arctic cold in much fo the Western Corn Belt, which should allow producers to market more of the hogs that were backed up because of the Christmas holiday and bitterly cold temperatures, they said.
Projected bearishness from the large supply could be offset by active buying from packers looking to expand slaughter on Saturday to make up for no activity on Wednesday, the dealers said.
Hog marketings Thursday in the interior Iowa and southern Minnesota areas had been slow early amid extreme cold and heavy overnight snowfall, they said.
Movement picked up as the day progressed, with one major packer in southern Minnesota saying they had the inventory they needed for Friday's slaughter.

Iowa/southern Minnesota hog prices Friday were seen steady-weak, with a top of $54.00 to $54.50 for hogs delivered to the plant. Illinois top plant prices could be up $0.50 at $53.50. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could be steady at $54.00.
